title: Power Pages: client APIs for scripting forms, lists, users and data
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents CLI automation for table permissions and site settings, although the briefing labels both automation surfaces undocumented. The suggested counting workaround is also wrong: adding $count=true does not remove the documented count limit.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Power Pages enforces table permissions on the server and the client API cannot override them.
claims.quote: Power Pages applies form metadata and table permissions on the server, and the client API can't override those settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Assigning table access to the Anonymous users web role makes the data accessible to any visitor.
claims.quote: When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/assign-table-permissions to sources; it directly states the anonymous-access warning.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: setVisible(false) only hides a control in the browser; table permissions and column security protect the data.
claims.quote: The `setVisible(false)` method hides a control in the browser only. Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: row.setVisible(false) changes the displayed list rather than the data returned by the server.
claims.quote: Hiding a row changes only what people see in the list; it doesn't change the data or the number of records that the server returns.

claims.claim: Client-side setDisabled changes do not override server-enforced restrictions.
claims.quote: When a control is locked on the server, such as a multiselect picklist on a read-only form or field, the `setDisabled(false)` method has no effect.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax requests include the session cookie.
claims.quote: **Credentials**: The session cookie is included with every request.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax automatically adds a CSRF token to every request.
claims.quote: **Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) token**: The token is retrieved when it's first needed, cached in memory, and added to the header of every request.

claims.claim: The documented signIn and signOut operations perform session navigation rather than configure identity providers.
claims.quote:
`signIn` | Redirects the user to the sign-in page.
`signOut` | Signs out the currently signed-in user.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited client API pages do not explicitly state whether Webapi table site settings gate $pages.webAPI.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API disable enable administrator site setting Webapi $pages.webAPI licensing. Read client-api/dataverse, client-api/examples and web-api-overview; the client API pages do not expressly discuss those settings.

claims.claim: Server logic and cloud flows triggered from page events run with no approval step.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API cloud flows approval step page events. Read client-api/ajax and cloud-flow-integration; they demonstrate invocation but do not guarantee that the called logic or flow has no approval step.
claims.fix: Replace the absolute statement with: 'Developers choose when scripts invoke these endpoints. Any approval or business checks depend on the called server logic or flow.'

claims.claim: getRecordCount returns at most 5,000.
claims.quote: The server returns a maximum count of 5,000. When a table contains more than 5,000 records, the result is 5,000.

claims.claim: A developer needing a total larger than 5,000 must use $count=true with retrieveMultipleRecords.
claims.quote: This option includes a count of rows that match the filter criteria, up to 5,000 for standard tables and 500 for elastic tables
claims.fix: Keep the documented getRecordCount cap, but replace the workaround with: 'retrieveMultipleRecords with $count=true returns records together with a count; it does not bypass the Dataverse count limit.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query/count-rows. The client API page recommends this option for records plus a count, not for a larger count.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Scope
claims.claim: Table permissions are managed in Power Pages design studio at Security > Table permissions.
claims.quote:
In the design studio on the side menu, select **Security**.
2. On the left pane in the **Protect** section, select **Table permissions** to add and modify table permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no CLI command or other automation for table permissions.
claims.quote: Support for download/upload of website configuration data to/from the local file system
claims.fix: Replace the undocumented automation side with the documented PAC CLI configuration workflow. The Supported tables section explicitly includes adx_entitypermission. Download the site, edit its table-permission YAML, and deploy using 'pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --modelVersion <1-or-2>'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/power-platform-cli and update the note and repeated prose; this is configuration deployment, not a dedicated permission-setting cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Site Settings is reachable from the editing experience through More items (...) > Portal Management > Site Settings.
claims.quote:
In the left side panel, select **More items** (**...**) > **Portal Management**.
3. Select **Site Settings** in the **Portal Management** app.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no automation for the Web API site settings.
claims.quote: In this file, you can have the table (entity) name with table ID, list of attributes, and the values that you want to override while uploading the portal configuration using the `deploymentProfile` parameter.
claims.fix: Replace the undocumented automation side with PAC CLI configuration deployment. This reference includes adx_sitesetting among supported tables and shows site-setting overrides in deployment YAML. Use 'pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --deploymentProfile <profile> --modelVersion <1-or-2>' after preparing the site's configuration/profile. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/power-platform-cli; retain the caveat that client API applicability is not explicitly stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages has capacity-based licensing measured in authenticated and anonymous users per website per month.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: **Authenticated users per website/month** and **Anonymous users per website/month**.

claims.claim: The separate portals Web API overview requires a Power Pages licence for its operations.
claims.quote: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages license.

claims.claim: The portals Web API overview says anonymous Web API calls count toward anonymous user capacity.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by anonymous users count towards the anonymous user capacity.

claims.claim: The portals Web API overview requires applicable authenticated user capacity licences for authenticated callers.
claims.quote: Web API calls made by authenticated users (internal or external) don't count towards page views, but require applicable authenticated user capacity licenses.

claims.claim: The client API references do not expressly explain whether the older portals Web API licensing statement applies unchanged to $pages.webAPI.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API $pages disable switch tenant site licensing pricing meter. Read client-api/dataverse, client API overview, web-api-overview and the Power Pages licensing FAQ; no explicit licensing cross-reference for $pages.webAPI was found.

claims.claim: Invoking Power Automate flows from Power Pages has its own licensing requirement.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents have their own licensing rather than a licence specified by the client API reference.

claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/client-api disable enable license prerequisites role. Read the seven cited client API references; none lists a prerequisite licence or administrator role.

claims.claim: If nobody acts, nothing breaks and all existing sites behave as before.
